title: Fuel Line
briefing: Case study, inspired by the 2021 ransomware attack that shut a major fuel pipeline. Quarrow Fuels, Valtren's sole fuel distributor, has stopped deliveries after a ransomware attack on its systems.
It expects to be down for six days. Amara Lindqvist has the fleet numbers; Mei Lin is asking how Quarrow was ever allowed to be a single point of failure.

evidence.title: Depot fuel
evidence.body: Diesel in depot tanks across the network: 120,000 litres.

evidence.title: Fleet consumption
evidence.body: The fleet uses 30,000 litres a day. Pharma routes account for 40% of it.

evidence.title: Quarrow notice
evidence.body: Deliveries suspended for an estimated six days. No secondary supplier is contracted.

questions.prompt: How many days can the fleet run at the normal rate on the fuel in the tanks?

mistakes.feedback: Six days is how long Quarrow expects to be down, not how long the fuel lasts.

questions.prompt: How many litres short is Valtren over the six-day outage at the normal rate?
questions.explanation: Six days x 30,000 = 180,000 needed; 180,000 - 120,000 in tanks = 60,000 litres short.

options.label: Prioritise pharma and contracted routes, cut non-critical runs and buy spot fuel from another distributor
options.feedback: Pharma routes alone use 12,000 litres a day, so the tanks cover them for ten days; spot purchases close the rest.

options.label: Run the full schedule and hope Quarrow is back early
options.feedback: On day five the trucks stop, including the pharma loads.

options.label: Offer to help Quarrow pay the ransom to speed things up
options.feedback: Not Valtren's call, possibly unlawful, and no guarantee it works.

options.label: Park the whole fleet to save fuel until deliveries resume
options.feedback: Saves fuel by breaking every contract, including the critical ones.

questions.prompt: Rate the risk of losing your only fuel supplier for several days, before treatment.
questions.explanation: Cyber attacks on suppliers are now common (possible); a fleet that stops within four days is a major impact.

questions.prompt: Which controls would have reduced the impact? Pick all that apply.

options.label: A contracted secondary fuel supplier
options.feedback: Removes the single point of failure.

options.label: A minimum days-of-fuel stock policy at depots
options.feedback: Buys time for any supplier problem.

options.label: Cyber resilience questions in supplier due diligence
options.feedback: Third-party cyber risk is your risk.

options.label: Valtren running its own refinery
options.feedback: Out of proportion to the risk.

lesson: Your supplier's cyber risk is your operational risk. Days of stock, a second source and triage of critical services keep the business moving.
